author: human
request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory narrows to one named specialty
summary: Both forms of the veterinarian directory, the paged page and the machine-readable list, narrow to the veterinarians holding one specialty named in the address, matched on the whole name ignoring case. The machine-readable list is reinstated as a supported surface under REQ-VET-004.
acceptance_criteria: [REQ-VET-003] /vets.html?specialty=<name> shows only the veterinarians holding that specialty; the page count and pagination apply to the filtered list.
[REQ-VET-003] On a filtered /vets.html page, every pagination link carries the specialty parameter, so moving between pages keeps the filter.
[REQ-VET-003] /vets?specialty=<name> returns the machine-readable document containing only the veterinarians holding that specialty.

[REQ-VET-003] Matching is on the whole specialty name, ignoring letter case, on both surfaces: a value differing only by case matches; a value matching only the beginning of a specialty name (for example 'radio') matches nothing.
[REQ-VET-003] A specialty value matching no veterinarian returns HTTP 200 with the usual page or document and an empty veterinarian list, on both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-003] An empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves exactly as if the parameter were absent, on both surfaces.
[REQ-VET-003] Edge case 3: a veterinarian holding no specialty never matches a named specialty, on either surface.
[REQ-VET-001] [REQ-VET-004] Without the parameter, /vets.html and /vets behave as today: the full paged directory and the full machine-readable list.
non_goals: Any form, dropdown, or other page control for choosing a specialty on either surface; a visible control may come as a follow-up request (intake decision 3).
Any other visible change to the directory page beyond pagination links carrying the parameter.
Narrowing by any attribute other than specialty, and free-text veterinarian search (NG-9 as narrowed).
Narrowing by more than one specialty in one request.
Prefix or partial matching of specialty names.
notes: ID mapping: REQ-VET-003 is the specialty narrowing (the intake's req_id). REQ-VET-004 is the fresh requirement intake decision 2 asks for, covering the reinstated machine-readable list; REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn. REQ-VET-004 needs no code change: its behavior exists and showResourcesVetList covers it, so it is batched here instead of a trivial slice of its own. NG-9 narrowed per intake decision 1: row, preamble, and non-goal ADR docs/adr/2026-09-11-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md. The ADR index row in docs/adr/README.md is outside product write scope. Design-owned text now stale: system-design.md known-defects row calling the machine-readable route requirement-less, the Contracts rows for Vets and VetController (now REQ-VET-004), and the Overview's no-JSON-API sentence. Open questions, narrowest reading taken and recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions: a real specialty name padded with spaces has no stated behavior; a visible control is deferred. The owner stated no further product answer will come during the work.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package and reuses the paged derived-query pattern owner search demonstrates: OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith with Pageable, and OwnerController.processFindForm's strip-then-query boundary step. No new module, type, pattern, or dependency. The adjustment: VetRepository gains two uncached specialty-narrowed reads, one paged (directory page) and one whole (JSON list), matching a Specialty's whole name ignoring case. VetController binds an optional request-scoped String, strips it, and selects the narrowed read when non-blank, otherwise today's cached read. vetList.html pagination links carry the value. Covering code resolved by direct read and grep of VetRepository.java, VetController.java, OwnerRepository.java:45, OwnerController.java:94 (IDE oracle not connected; weaker basis). Design memory: system-design.md section Contracts (VetRepository, VetController, Vets, Vet, Specialty, CacheConfiguration rows; vet-cache invariant), Overview, Security Context, Threat Model; ADR 2026-09-11-specialty-narrowing-as-uncached-repository-query.
integration_points: Entry point GET /vets.html binds the specialty as an optional request-scoped String request parameter beside the existing int page. No persisted type is bound and no data binder is involved (security-principles section Realization, Mass assignment row: nothing to disallow).
Entry point GET /vets binds the specialty as an optional request-scoped String request parameter and returns the Vets wrapper filled from the whole narrowed read. It stays unpaged (PRD non-goal).

Repository boundary in ClinicServiceTests: real implementation, no double. The existing Spring Data slice test runs against H2 seed data. Matching semantics are tested here once: whole name ignoring case ('RADIOLOGY' matches Helen Leary and Henry Stevens), a prefix ('radio') matches nothing, an unknown name yields empty, specialty-less vets (James Carter, Sharon Jenkins) never match, and the paged read's total counts only matches (testing-principles section Stop Re-Testing Other Units).

Repository boundary in VetControllerTests: framework stub, extending the class's existing @MockitoBean VetRepository with given(...) stubs for the narrowed reads. Reason: that existing stub already fills the VetRepository bean slot in the @WebMvcTest context, so a hand-written double would give one boundary two doubles in one class. A real repository cannot supply more than five vets of one specialty for the paging test, since the repository is read-only and the seed holds at most two per specialty. Controller tests assert binding, stripping, blank-means-absent delegation (which read answers), model attributes, link rendering, and the JSON body, not matching semantics.
HTTP transport: MockMvc, the sanctioned harness (testing-principles section Mocking Policy), for both surfaces.

vetList.html: every pagination link (numbered, first, previous, next, last) carries the stripped specialty as a Thymeleaf link-expression parameter, for example @{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}. On an unfiltered page, no link carries a specialty parameter, so REQ-VET-001 behavior is unchanged.

patterns.description: Paged Spring Data derived query taking a Pageable: the shape of the narrowed paged read.
Boundary step: strip the search value and treat blank as the broadest search. The specialty value follows it.
findPaginated's local page size: the narrowed paged read uses the same value, one page size for both directory forms (system-design.md section Constants).

risks.risk: Case-insensitive matching left to column collation reproduces the owner-search defect: PostgreSQL stores specialty names case-sensitively.
risks.mitigation: The derived query folds case on both sides (IgnoreCase on an equality predicate, e.g. findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase). Never StartingWith, Containing, or Like: prefix matching is a PRD non-goal. Cites system-design.md section Known Defects (PostgreSQL owner search row) and the ADR.

risks.risk: Every other VetRepository read carries @Cacheable("vets"); copying it onto the narrowed reads makes a caller-supplied string a key in an unbounded cache.
risks.mitigation: The narrowed reads carry no cache annotation. Cites system-design.md section Contracts (vet-cache invariant), section Threat Model (caller-chosen cache-key row), the ADR, and design-validation Reliability by Design (resource limits).

risks.risk: The template's existing links use __${...}__ preprocessing and string concatenation. Copying that for the specialty would run a request-derived value through Thymeleaf preprocessing (expression injection) and skip URL encoding.
risks.mitigation: The specialty reaches links only as a link-expression parameter, which URL-encodes and attribute-escapes it. Cites security-principles section Realization (Injection and Cross-site scripting rows) and system-design.md section Threat Model (XSS row).

risks.risk: Filtering or paging in memory over the cached full list puts the matching rule and paging arithmetic in VetController.
risks.mitigation: The controller only strips, tests blank, and selects a read; matching and paging live in the query. Cites architecture-principles section Pattern Catalog (Web controller row) and its checklist item on new controller rules; the ADR records the rejected option.

risks.risk: Joining specialties for the predicate can repeat a vet and skew the page count, and a JOIN FETCH on the EAGER many-to-many would force in-memory pagination.
risks.mitigation: Distinct in the derived query; the predicate join is never a fetch join. If a hand-written @Query is needed, it is parameterized JPQL. Cites system-design.md section Persistence (eager association fetch, open-in-view off), security-principles section Realization (Injection row), and the prd-entry criterion that the page count covers only matches.

risks.risk: A real specialty name padded with spaces has no stated behavior (docs/prd.md Open Questions).
risks.mitigation: The design strips the value as owner search does, so a padded name matches (system-design.md section Contracts, VetController row). No test pins the padded case, which keeps the open question reversible.

risks.risk: Without the parameter, either surface drifts from today's behavior.
risks.mitigation: An absent or blank value selects today's cached reads unchanged. showVetListHtml and showResourcesVetList stay green (prd-entry criterion for REQ-VET-001 and REQ-VET-004).

notes: Autofix audit: the log holds no design-doc-autofix records. Suggested test placement: ClinicServiceTests (real H2) takes theSpecialtyFilterShouldMatchTheWholeNameIgnoringCase, theSpecialtyFilterShouldNotMatchAVetHoldingNoSpecialty, and the repository half of theSpecialtyFilterShouldYieldAnEmptyListWhenNoVetMatches. VetControllerTests (MockMvc plus the existing stub) takes theVetDirectoryShouldListOnlyVetsHoldingTheRequestedSpecialty, theVetDirectoryShouldPaginateTheFilteredList (stub a narrowed page whose total spans several pages), theVetDirectoryPaginationLinksShouldCarryTheSpecialty, theVetListResourceShouldReturnOnlyVetsHoldingTheRequestedSpecialty, theSpecialtyFilterShouldBeIgnoredWhenBlank on both surfaces, and the HTTP-200 half of the empty case. Product-expert handover items done: ADR index row for the non-goal ADR; the stale Known Defects row on the machine-readable route removed; the Vets and VetController Contracts rows now cite REQ-VET-004; the Overview no-JSON-API sentence rewritten. The non-goal ADR file itself is the product expert's write; this dispatch wrote only its index row. Brief gap for its owner: security-principles section Realization has no row naming template preprocessing of a request-derived value as an injection vector; the Injection and XSS rows are the nearest. That brief is outside this agent's write scope. Pre-existing, not this slice's work: the unfiltered paged read caches every requested page number (Threat Model row, Partial).

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the request-derived specialty reaches the database only through the Spring Data derived queries findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) and findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) (VetRepository.java diff), which bind the value as a parameter. The IgnoreCase keyword on a simple property is an equality match, not LIKE, so '%' and '_' carry no wildcard meaning (derived-query semantics, not exercised by a wildcard-specific test). The diff contains no @Query, createQuery, or nativeQuery (grep over the scripts/changeset.sh diff returned no such added line).

Cross-site scripting on the directory page: vetList.html passes the specialty only as a link-expression parameter, e.g. line 30 `@{/vets.html(page=${i},specialty=${specialty})}`. Thymeleaf URL-encodes the parameter value and attribute-escapes the th:href output. `grep -F -e 'utext' -e '__$' -- src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html` returns no match, so the change adds no unescaped output and no preprocessing of request text. It also removes the four old `__${...}__` preprocessing uses from the pagination links. VetControllerTests.theVetDirectoryPaginationLinksShouldNeverEchoAMarkupCarryingSpecialty sends the payload `">` and asserts the response never contains it verbatim.

Cache-key growth: both new repository methods carry no @Cacheable. Their Javadoc reads 'Uncached: the caller chooses the name, so it must never key the vets cache', so a caller cannot grow the unbounded vets cache by varying the specialty. The unfiltered paged read keeps its caching on page numbers, which system-design.md § Threat Model already records as Partial. The change does not extend that surface.

Exposed surface and binding: the diff adds no route. It adds one optional @RequestParam String specialty (default "") to the two existing vet GET handlers, which only read data. It binds no @ModelAttribute or @RequestBody object, so no mass-assignment surface is added. system-design.md § Security Context (line 163) records the new input. The value is only stripped and length-bounded by the servlet container's request-line limit, which is adequate because every sink (bind parameter, encoded link) is safe for arbitrary text.

Secrets and logging: the diff adds no credential, logger call, or System.out (grep for password|secret|token|apikey|credential|log.|logger|System.out over the added lines of scripts/changeset.sh matched only the system-design.md prose line naming datasource credentials from environment variables). It also adds no new exception message that could reach the error page.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set (scripts/changeset.sh --name-only), so no dependency changed. No OWASP dependencyCheckAnalyze task is configured (grep of build.gradle for dependencyCheck returned none), so no NVD match ran in this review. The resolved runtimeClasspath shows Spring Boot 4.1.1, jackson-databind (tools.jackson.core) 3.1.5, Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE, and Hibernate ORM 7.4.5.Final.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow both vet list routes by a whole-name specialty

blast_radius.note: Everything stays inside the vet feature: VetController, VetRepository, vetList.html, and their two test classes, plus owner-requested doc records. The new security-surface input reaches only bound derived-query parameters and URL-encoded Thymeleaf link parameters, which I checked in the hunks. The 45 hunks are mostly docs and test imports. The tree the reviewers saw (fa46501) is the tree graded here.

semantic_surprise.note: The branch directions are correct: an empty name falls through to the cached findAll and a non-empty one to the narrowed read, on both routes. The query is IgnoreCase equality, never StartingWith or Like. The template adds a specialty only when the model attribute is non-null. The rewritten unfiltered links render the same /vets.html?page=N as the old __${i}__ form. The narrowed reads carry no @Cacheable, matching the ADR. One judgment call: stripping means a padded name like ' radiology ' matches. The PRD still lists this as an open question, but system-design.md records it as design.

test_adequacy.note: Matching rules are tested against the real H2 repository and seed data: case variants, prefix rejection, no match, vets with no specialty, and the paged total counting only matches. Controller tests pin the exact PageRequest, the model attributes, the encoded filtered links, blank-means-absent on both routes, and the JSON body. Three gaps, none affecting today's behavior: no test pins that the narrowed reads stay uncached, no test checks that a padded non-blank name is stripped, and the unfiltered REQ-VET-001 links are not asserted after the template rewrite.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers in the high-risk full-battery plan approved on the first pass with no findings. The test and code-quality recommendations are first-round polish: a brittle substring assertion, the untested uncached invariant, and a ternary repeated in five links. The missing OWASP scanner is a standing project gap. The citations I checked resolve (system-design.md:80/103/104/181, prd.md:119, the ADR at line 38, VetRepository.java:58-78); only the test reviewer's blank-test range drifts slightly.

scope_deviation.note: The intake-decision states each doc change as the owner's decision: narrowing NG-9, reinstating /vets as REQ-VET-004 while REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn, a URL-only contract, and pagination links carrying the parameter. The code adds no page control and no other filter attribute. Build retries, consultations, and design revisions are all 0.

rationale: The hunks match the owner's recorded contract: whole-name case-insensitive equality, blank means absent, uncached narrowed reads, and encoded pagination links. The tests exercise real outcomes. A glance is enough; to go further, confirm the NG-9 and REQ-VET-004 PRD wording and decide whether padded names should match.
